title: Players on New Teams
brief: Which players changed teams, and is their value likely to rise or fall in the new usage and minutes picture? It must reflect that new-team players often dip in year one unless minutes rise, and flag ripple effects on teammates.
summary: Players who change teams usually lose some value in year one, and that includes stars. The exception is a player whose minutes rise in the new role. In our auction, bid stars at the low end of their fair range and pay full fair value only for players with a clearly bigger role, such as Paul George and Naz Reid. Leave back-end players from rebuilt rosters on waivers, and watch the teammates whose minutes these moves open or close.

paragraphs.text: The notes agree on the default. When a good player moves to a new team, his production usually dips. Stars are no exception. Players often take a hit in their first year while they adjust, and growing pains are normal.

For our auction, do not pay last season's price for a moved player unless his minutes are set to rise. Jaylen Brown is the clearest case. His 29 USD in our league last season paid for a 36% usage role he no longer has, so the fair range is now 20 to 24 USD. Ja Morant cost 17 USD last season, and experts now value him near 5 USD.

Brown's note expects growing pains in October and November to hold his scoring down. So a slow first month from a moved star is what the notes predict. Check his minutes before you react. If the minutes are where they should be, a slow start fits the adjustment pattern and is not a reason to sell.
More minutes on the new team can offset the adjustment hit. Judge last season's rank in context: role, teammates, injuries and minutes. A change in usage and minutes can raise a player's value a lot.

Likely risers have a bigger role. Paul George should be Boston's number two option, and experts call 10 to 15 USD good value. Naz Reid is fair at 10 to 14 USD if he plays 31 or more minutes at power forward and takes more than last season's 11.3 shots. Peyton Watson has a secure 30-minute starting job at a last-dollar price. John Collins starts at power forward in Detroit, but his upside is small.

Usage alone is not enough. A player who moves from a good team to a bad one can see his usage rise while his playing time falls. A player who moves to a deeper team can lose usage and still gain value, because his minutes and role become more stable. Norman Powell should be Chicago's top usage option, and Julius Randle's usage should rise toward 30 in Brooklyn. Still, check that Randle holds near 32 minutes and that Powell keeps his share next to Caleb Wilson.

Likely fallers have fewer minutes or a smaller role. Morant may come off the bench for 27 to 28 minutes behind Lillard, Holiday and Henderson. DeRozan projects for about 29 bench minutes. Vučević is now Wendell Carter Jr.'s backup. Tobias Harris likely comes off the bench. Miles Bridges needs a big shot share next to Booker, Jalen Green and Brooks. Bennedict Mathurin's projected volume drops to 8.2 shots on a crowded Pelicans team.

The experts disagree on how much weight the dip deserves. One side treats it as the default for anyone who moves, stars included. The other side says a new role can raise value a lot, and that a deeper team can help through more stable minutes. Both sides use minutes as the deciding check. In practice, bid moved stars at the low end of their range. Do not discount players whose minutes are clearly going up.

Teams with heavy roster turnover tend to be rocky in year one. It goes more smoothly when the main core stays. Adding stars to existing stars has historically been choppy at first. Our list has three such cases: Philadelphia adds LeBron James and Brown next to Embiid, Boston adds George next to Tatum, and Minnesota adds LaMelo Ball next to Edwards.

On rebuilt teams, coaches may try a setup for about 15 games and then reverse it, so back-end players there are uncertain. By our list, Philadelphia has six new players and Milwaukee has five. Miami, the Clippers and the Lakers have four each. Pay no more than 1 USD for back-end players from these teams, such as Jaime Jaquez Jr., Rui Hachimura and Sandro Mamukelashvili. Treat a new starter on these teams as a 15-game trial. Do not spend big FAB after one hot week.
A move also changes the picture for the player's new teammates and for the team he left. Track these knock-on roles as closely as the moved player himself.

Giannis trade. Milwaukee's backcourt is crowded. Tyler Herro needs 34 to 35 minutes. Jaquez has to keep his starting spot and his assists while Herro and Rollins handle the ball. Kasparas Jakučionis is fighting Gary Trent Jr. for a rotation spot. Kel'el Ware's value depends on whether Taylor Jenkins starts him next to Myles Turner. In Miami, Bobby Portis gets the minutes behind Giannis and Bam Adebayo, and Tim Hardaway Jr. may take starter minutes from Klay Thompson.

LaMelo Ball deal. The check on Ball is whether his usage and assists hold up next to Edwards. In Charlotte, Reid moves into power forward minutes. Coby White and Kon Knueppel are injured, which opens short-term minutes for Grayson Allen and Royce O'Neale. Both are only three-point streamers.

Kawhi Leonard deal. Brandon Ingram is out with a partially torn Achilles until somewhere between Thanksgiving and Christmas. While he is out, Hachimura has a chance at 30-plus minutes and more shots, and Max Strus may get his assists back near 4. Their chance depends on Ingram being out. Gradey Dick is likely out of the rotation.

Backup bigs only matter when the starter sits. If Walker Kessler gets hurt, Mamukelashvili is the first Lakers center to add, then Kevon Looney. The same applies to Deandre Ayton when Davis is out, Marvin Bagley III when Jokic is out, Isaiah Stewart when Edey is out and Vučević when Carter is out. Ariel Hukporti's season-ending injury leaves Philadelphia thin behind Embiid, but experts expect no useful fill-in there. Leave these players on waivers and save FAB to add them the day an injury hits.

In the first two to three weeks, compare each moved player's minutes with his projection. The targets are: Giannis 32 to 33, Ball 30 to 32, Brown 36 or more, Reid 31 or more, Herro 34 to 35, Randle about 32 and Ware above 25. A player who reaches his target is past the main risk. A player who falls short is a candidate to sell or drop before the dip shows up in your weekly matchups.

Watch for trades before the 2027-03-04 deadline. If Powell is moved to a contender, his value drops right before our playoffs. Herro and Jaquez also have trade talk to watch. A player traded at the deadline starts a new adjustment just as weeks 19 to 21 begin. Brooklyn may rest Randle in March, during our playoffs.
